passage:
In the school hall after assembly, Ayesha held up her shiny helper-of-the-week badge. "Look, Rehan!"
Rehan's smile faded and he looked at the floor. The badge felt heavier in her hand. She did not know why he was sad.
Keerthana, the teacher, watched from the doorway and said nothing.
Ayesha thought for a moment. "You can get one too. What are you making today?"
"A clay elephant," Rehan mumbled.
"Can I see it?"
He brightened a little and led her to the shelf.

qa.q: What did Ayesha hold up in the hall?
qa.a: She held up her shiny helper-of-the-week badge.

qa.q: How does Ayesha feel when Rehan looks at the floor?
qa.a: She feels confused: she does not know why he is sad, and the badge suddenly feels heavier.

qa.q: What did Ayesha do that kept the friendship warm?
qa.a: She told him he could get one too and asked about his own clay elephant, so the moment was about him as well.

qa.q: How might Rehan see Ayesha's badge at first?
qa.a: He seems sad and perhaps envious, since his smile fades and he looks away from it.

grounding: A child shows her badge and her friend looks away sadly; she is confused, then says he can get one too and asks about his work.

passage: At the swimming club in Lisbon, Omar got a gold badge for his first width. He ran to his friend Tomás, waving it. "Look! I got a badge!" Tomás looked at it, then looked away at the pool. His mouth turned down. Omar stopped. He felt muddled. Why was Tomás sad? Their coach, Ada, was nearby. Omar thought, then said, "You can get one too. You kick really fast. What did you do today?" Tomás looked up. "I put my face in the water for the first time." "Whoa! That's hard!" Tomás smiled a little. Omar put his badge in his pocket.

qa.q: What did Omar get a badge for?
qa.a: He got a gold badge for his first width.

qa.q: How did Omar feel when Tomás looked away?
qa.a: He felt confused and muddled, not understanding why his friend was sad.

qa.q: What did Omar do that shares pride without bragging?
qa.a: He told Tomás he could get one too, asked about Tomás's own progress and put the badge away.

qa.q: How might Tomás feel when Omar asks about his day?
qa.a: He may feel noticed and a little proud, instead of left behind.

grounding: A young boy shows his badge and his friend looks away sadly; he encourages his friend and asks about his work instead of bragging.

passage: In the school corridor after assembly, Darshan held up his shiny "Star Reader" badge. "Imran, look!" Imran glanced at it and turned away, kicking the wall softly. His eyes were shiny. Darshan's smile faded. He didn't understand. Had he done something wrong? Then he remembered Imran's reading book was still on the yellow level. Darshan put the badge in his pocket. "You can get one too. You read the dragon book really well yesterday." Imran sniffed. "I got stuck on two words." "I got stuck on five!" Imran almost laughed. They walked to class together.

qa.q: How did Darshan feel when Imran turned away?
qa.a: He felt confused and worried, wondering if he had done something wrong.

qa.q: How did Darshan keep the friendship warm?
qa.a: He put the badge away, told Imran he could get one too and praised Imran's own reading.

qa.q: What is it like for Imran when Darshan shows the badge?
qa.a: It stings; he feels sad and left behind because his own reading is slower.

grounding: A young boy shows his reading badge and his friend turns away sadly; he encourages his friend and talks about his work instead of bragging.
